### Pre-submit Checks

- [x] I have [searched Warp bugs](https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3ABUG) and there are no duplicates
- [x] I have [searched Warp known issues page](https://docs.warp.dev/help/known-issues) and my issue is not there
- [ ] I have an issue with AI and have included the debugging ID (Optional, but helps expedite the AI quality fix). [Debugging ID instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/agent-platform/agent/ai-faqs#gathering-ai-debugging-id)
- [ ] I have technical issue and have included the logs (optional, but helps expedite the bug fix). [Log instructions](https://docs.warp.dev/support-and-community/troubleshooting-and-support/sending-us-feedback#gathering-warp-logs)

### Describe the bug

`ctrl+y` does "delete all left" on linux and you need to unbind it for paste from internal clipboard to work. 

meaning by default I don't see any easy way to paste from internal clipboard (therefore commands like `ctrl+u` are useless by default)

### To reproduce

1. put some text into the terminal field
2. pres ctrl+y -> it will delete the test to the left)
3. clear the ctrl+y binding
4. put some text into the field again
5. press ctrl+u
6. press ctrl+y -> it will paste from internal buffer (what ctrl+u deleted)

### Expected behavior

At least warn a user about this in some way. 
Or let user change the internal "hard-coded" bindings.

### Screenshots, videos, and logs

_No response_

### Operating system (OS)

Linux

### Operating system and version

6.18.32-1-MANJARO

### Shell Version

zsh 5.9 (x86_64-pc-linux-gnu)

### Current Warp version

v0.2026.05.20.09.21.stable_03

### Regression

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp

### Recent working Warp date

_No response_

### Additional context

The issue seem to be these pieces of code.

fixedbinding for yank: https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/blob/c37c1cd6ec75726ea297131bab2b2b0b19ecce60/app/src/editor/view/mod.rs#L266

editable binding for delete-all-left: https://github.com/warpdotdev/warp/blob/c37c1cd6ec75726ea297131bab2b2b0b19ecce60/app/src/editor/view/mod.rs#L804

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

No

### Is this an issue only in Warp?

Yes, I confirmed that this only happens in Warp, not other terminals.

### Describe the bug

```shell
Whenever I elevate my rights to root through SSH I cannot use either the OPTION or CMD with ARROW LEFT/RIGHT or  to either skip the whole word, skip to the end/start of the line or deleting the next/previous word or the whole line.
```


### To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce:
1. SSH to a RHEL based server(havn't tested on anything else) as normal user(needs wheel permissions)
2. Execute `sudo su -` to elevate to root
3. Write something like "asdf qwerty"
4. Try to use 'CMD+ARROW-LEFT' 
5. You can also try to 'CMD+BACKSPACE'
6. Also you can try to 'OPTION+ARROW-LEFT'
7. You could also move the cursor to the start of the line and do the commands with ARROW-RIGHT or DELETEKEY


### Expected behaviour

```shell
4. When having the cursor at the end of the line this should skip both words and get back to the start of the line
5. When having the cursor at the end of the line this should delete the whole line
6. When having the cursor at the end of the line this move the cursor to the first letter in the second word(in my example it should move the cursor in front of q)
```


### Screenshots

MacOS

12.2.1

<!-- warp-feedback-skill:v1 -->
## Summary
Add a setting to configure which characters are treated as word boundaries for word-deletion shortcuts such as Delete Word Left.

## Problem
Delete Word Left currently treats filesystem paths and similar tokens as a single word, deleting backward only to whitespace.

## Reproduction steps or desired workflow
1. Type text containing path-like delimiters, for example `/var/www/example.com/logs`.
2. Trigger Delete Word Left.
3. Observe that deletion jumps to the previous space instead of stopping at path delimiters.
4. Desired workflow: let users configure delimiter characters (for example `/`, `.`, `-`, `_`) so word-based deletion shortcuts stop at those boundaries.

## Artifacts
None attached.

## Warp version
Unknown

## Operating system
macOS

items.body:
### Discord username (optional)

_No response_

### Describe the bug

The `Cut All Left` keyboard shortcut does not appear to do anything when pressed.

I wanted to unbind `Ctrl+U` from `Copy and Clear Selected Lines` and bind it to `Cut All Left`, but I also tried other bindings to no avail.

### To reproduce

1. Open settings
2. Navigate to Keyboard shortcuts
3. Search the commands for "Cut All Left"
4. Bind to `<unused-keybind>` (or Ctrl + U, and unbind it from "Copy and Clear Selected Lines")
5. Close settings
6. Type some characters at terminal prompt
7. Move cursor left (To ensure its only removing characters from the left rather than whole line)
8. Press bound key

### Expected behavior

All characters left of the cursor should be cut/deleted.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Operating system

Linux

### Operating system and version

Fedora 39

### Shell Version

zsh 5.9

### Current Warp version

v0.2024.03.12.08.02.stable_01

### Regression

No, this bug or issue has existed throughout my experience using Warp

### Recent working Warp date

_No response_

### Additional context

I'm using X11 and I have the following in my `.zshrc`:

```zsh
bindkey \^u backward-kill-line
```

### Does this block you from using Warp daily?

No

### Is this a Warp specific issue? (i.e. does it happen in Terminal, iTerm, Kitty, etc.)

Yes, this I confirmed this only happens in Warp, not other terminals.
